I got two tablets sent to me, but I only need one. I want to return the pricier one

observed_facts.fact: The user initially stated they received two tablets across the conversation context, but actually they had only received two tablets total across different orders or meant something else; user says 'I got two tablets sent to me, but I only need one. I want to return the pricier one'.

When told the refund could not go to the credit card for the specific order, the simulated user abruptly changed their mind and demanded to return both entire orders (all items in both orders, or both tablets depending on interpretation).

inference.inference: According to the system instructions/reference solution, the user's instruction in step 20 ('return both tablets from those orders') was interpreted by the agent as returning the individual tablet items from the two respective orders, whereas the reference solution expected all items in order #W9571698 to be returned when the user got angry and said 'return everything on that order' (in the user prompt persona description: 'return everything on that order and refund to GC'). The user's vague phrasing in step 20 ('return both tablets') caused the agent to return only the single tablet item per order rather than all items in order #W9571698.
